name: Is it better to do a rear addition or a full remodel?

mainEntity.name: When does a rear-house addition make more sense than reconfiguring the whole house through a full remodel?
mainEntity.text: When does a rear-house addition make more sense than reconfiguring the whole house through a full remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision usually comes down to whether the home needs more space or just better space. A rear addition is ideal when the property can support extra square footage and the goal is to create a larger kitchen, primary suite, family room, or more seamless backyard access. A full remodel can be the better option when the current footprint is already adequate but poorly arranged, because you may gain more value by improving circulation, light, and room relationships without increasing the building envelope. Rear additions are typically more expensive and more permit-intensive than many interior remodels, but they can also produce a more dramatic lifestyle change. The right choice depends on the lot, zoning, budget, and whether the house is worth expanding. Homeowners should compare both options side by side before starting design, because the best solution is not always the largest one.
acceptedAnswer.description: A rear addition makes sense when you need more square footage or a better indoor-outdoor connection. A full remodel is often better when the existing layout is inefficient and the house can be improved without enlarging the footprint.
